Today this is a **vendor-neutral `TaxPreparation::TaxAutomations` core with namespace-based adapters**, still sharing some legacy Juno storage. **Instead is the only registered adapter.** GruntWorx already has a provider enum value, but that does not make it an operational integration.

**Vendor-neutral ports**

The core owns application policy, shared records, validation and lifecycle orchestration:

| Area | Core services and responsibilities |
|---|---|
| Connect | `Authorizations::Create` starts authorization; `Connections::Create` finishes it and switches providers. |
| Connection lifecycle | `Connections::Find`, `Disconnect`, `DisconnectAll`, `Renew`, `Revoke`, `VerifyGrant`. |
| Export | `ExportAsync` authorizes, validates files against capabilities, creates shared records, then delegates delivery. |
| Status handling | `Documents::UpdateStatus`, `FailUpload`, `BroadcastStatus`; adapters translate vendor statuses into the shared vocabulary. |
| Recovery | Resume sends after reconnect; periodic reconciliation of uploaded files awaiting processing results. |
| Data lifecycle | Preparation deletion, contact merging, firm deactivation and destruction. |
| Form support | `TaxPreparationPrefills::Find` reads shared history and firm settings without requiring a live connection. |

The export boundary is explicit: the core hands the adapter a preparation and shared document records; the adapter owns the delivery workflow. See [export orchestration](/Users/Shared/nav-ab/repo-master/app/services/tax_preparation/tax_automations/export_async.rb:53).

**Registration and adapter contract**

[Registry](/Users/Shared/nav-ab/repo-master/app/lib/tax_preparation/tax_automations/registry.rb:3) contains:

```ruby
ADAPTERS = {instead: TaxPreparation::TaxAutomations::Instead}.freeze
FEATURE_FLAGS = {instead: :tax_automations_instead}.freeze
```

Selection usually follows `FirmSettings.provider`. Authorization explicitly names the target provider, allowing a switch while settings still point at the previous vendor. Historical/background work can resolve a provider independently or iterate all registered adapters. A provider without a feature-flag entry is offered to every firm.

The contract is implemented through constant lookup and method calls. Production dispatch requires an adapter namespace to expose:

| Member | Required interface |
|---|---|
| `Connection` | ActiveRecord model supporting `.for_firm(firm)`, `.usable_for(firm)`, `.capabilities`, lifecycle scopes and ordinary queries such as `.find`, `.where`, `.connected`, `.installed`. |
| `Client` | `.new(connection)`; token renewal and revocation through `TokenRefreshable`. The shared signed-upload path also calls `upload_to_signed_target`. |
| `Authorizations::Create` | `.call(user, actor, provider, return_url)` |
| `Connections::Create` | `.call(user, actor, provider, params)` |
| `ExportAsync` | `.call(user, actor, tax_preparation, tax_automation_documents:)` |
| `Documents::ReconcileStatusesAsync` | `.call(user, actor, connection, {tax_automation_document_ids: …})` |
| `DestroyForTaxPreparations` | `.call(user, actor, firm_id, tax_preparations)` |
| `DestroyForFirm` | `.call(user, actor, firm_id)` |
| `MergeForContact` | `.call(user, actor, firm_id, source_contact_id, target_contact_id)` |

These services return the shared service-result convention. The reconciliation requirement comes from the [background sweep](/Users/Shared/nav-ab/repo-master/app/workers/tax_preparation/tax_automations/documents/reconcile_sweep_worker.rb:21), so implementing only authorization and export would leave the adapter incomplete.

The current reusable connection contract is **OAuth-oriented**. [HasOauthConnection](/Users/Shared/nav-ab/repo-master/app/models/concerns/tax_preparation/tax_automations/has_oauth_connection.rb:26) supplies encrypted credentials, expiry handling and states `disconnected`, `connected`, `expired`, `revoked`. Both connected and expired grants are usable because refresh may recover an expired grant.

`BaseClient` supplies shared transport/error infrastructure and includes `TokenRefreshable`. Its required hooks are `base_url`, `auth_headers` and `vendor_error_message`; OAuth endpoints and credentials are declared with `.oauth2_settings`. Vendor-specific error classification and rate-limit grouping have optional hooks.

**Capability passport**

The passport describes **the vendor**, rather than a particular connection. It is available through `Connection.capabilities` without fetching a connection row.

[HasCapabilities](/Users/Shared/nav-ab/repo-master/app/models/tax_preparation/tax_automations/has_capabilities.rb:18) builds a validated `Dry::Struct` containing:

- `terms`: one entry per return type, with `return_type`, `accepted_file_formats`, `max_file_size_mb`.
- `supported_tax_years`.

Adapters implement private class methods `capability_terms` and `supported_tax_years`. Several return types may share one declared group of terms; duplicate claims are rejected. Extensions must be lowercase alphanumeric strings, size limits positive integers, and years between 2000 and the current year plus one. Missing implementations and malformed values fail when `.capabilities` is evaluated.

The passport drives server-side export validation. File-size limits use Rails `.megabytes`, i.e. **1,048,576 bytes per declared MB**. API serialization exposes:

```text
capabilities:
  tax_years: [...]
  return_types:
    - value, name, type
      file_types, file_size_limit
```

Here `type` is `personal` or `business`. See [passport serialization](/Users/Shared/nav-ab/repo-master/app/serializers/tax_preparation/base/tax_automations/connection_serializer.rb:57).

Instead currently derives supported forms from its entity mapping, uses configured formats/size limits, and accepts the current tax year plus the preceding two years.

**Data model**

| Entity | Role and keys |
|---|---|
| `FirmSettings` | One per firm. Stores selected provider and external-account binding (`external_tenant_uuid`). Provider values: `juno: 0`, `gruntworx: 1`, `instead: 2`. |
| `TaxAutomations::TaxPreparation` | Shared return envelope: firm, client/account, optional contact, year, return type, EIN and business name. Core identity is **firm + client + contact + year**; changing return type reuses the envelope. |
| `TaxAutomations::Document` | Shared send record linking a source document to an envelope. Unique by **firm + preparation + source document + provider + return type**. Provider and return type are snapshots taken at send time. |
| `Instead::Connection` | One grant per firm, creator, encrypted tokens, expiry/lifecycle fields and Instead-specific PKCE ceremony fields. |
| `Instead::Entity` | Vendor taxpayer identity, including external UUID, entity type, client/contact linkage, source and synchronization/archive metadata. |
| `Instead::Document` | Vendor details for one shared send record: Instead entity, external file UUID and path. One-to-one with the shared send record. |

The shared send record owns two separate state machines:

- Upload: `waiting → uploading → uploaded`, with failure/reset paths.
- Processing: `sent`, `processing`, `processed`, `error`, `archived`, `exceeded`.

It also stores normalized failure reasons and `uploaded_at`; these do not belong in vendor-specific document tables. See [shared document model](/Users/Shared/nav-ab/repo-master/app/models/tax_preparation/tax_automations/document.rb:3).

Two details matter when assessing GruntWorx:

- **Provider switching preserves historical ownership.** Settings change only when the new connection completes; send records retain their original provider. Cleanup can therefore reach multiple vendors.
- **The Juno transition remains incomplete.** The shared preparation model still uses `juno_tax_preparations`, retains Juno associations and legacy query behavior, while new core rows use their own client/contact columns. Juno is explicitly excluded from the adapter registry pending its move behind these ports. See [preparation model](/Users/Shared/nav-ab/repo-master/app/models/tax_preparation/tax_automations/tax_preparation.rb:11).

No files were edited.
